name: Government
title: Public service application completeness desk
summary: Assemble application evidence and service-rule citations for accountable caseworker review with accessible applicant communication.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A municipal agency receives applications for a community assistance program through online and paper channels. Caseworkers must identify missing documents, locate applicable published rules, and communicate next steps. Agents support intake and evidence organization; authorized officials retain eligibility, benefit, and appeal decisions.
problem: Applicants use different languages and document formats, and records may be incomplete for legitimate reasons. Treating an absent document as an adverse fact can unfairly constrain access. Rules also vary by program version and application date.
whyAgents: Document intake, rule retrieval, evidence completeness, and communication specialists separate extraction from judgment. A case workflow preserves applicants' submitted evidence, tracks unanswered questions, and routes decisions to accountable officials.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure caseworker preparation and applicant comprehension alongside correction burden. The workflow should make public-service processes more legible while avoiding automated determinations or unsupported claims of regulatory compliance.

agents.name: Document intake agent
agents.responsibility: Extract submitted fields with page references and uncertainty labels.
agents.boundary: Cannot alter original submissions or infer missing personal circumstances.

agents.name: Program rule agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve published requirements effective for the application date.
agents.boundary: Cannot create eligibility rules or decide exceptions.

agents.name: Completeness reviewer
agents.responsibility: Compare available evidence with the official application checklist.
agents.boundary: Missing evidence remains a question, not an automatic denial.

agents.name: Applicant communication agent
agents.responsibility: Draft clear next-step notices in the requested supported language.
agents.boundary: Officials approve decisions and notices; the agent cannot send adverse determinations.

systems.name: Case management system
systems.role: Owns application identifiers, assignments, official decisions, and review history.

systems.name: Document and policy repositories
systems.role: Store original submissions and published rule versions with access and retention controls.

systems.name: Applicant service portal
systems.role: Supports accessible communication, document requests, and status tracking without exposing internal protected notes.

flow.title: Register application
flow.description: Deduplicate submission attempts and preserve receipt time, channel, language preference, and the applicant's original documents.

flow.title: Authorize case access
flow.description: Resolve program, staff assignment, and purpose before retrieving supporting records from other agency systems.

flow.title: Extract evidence carefully
flow.description: Capture document fields with page references; mark illegible or uncertain text for staff review rather than completing it speculatively.

flow.title: Check published requirements
flow.description: Apply the correct checklist version and distinguish missing, unavailable, and disputed evidence in the case packet.

flow.title: Review applicant notice
flow.description: Present officials with cited requirements and a draft request for clarification that explains the available next steps.

flow.title: Record accountable action
flow.description: Save the approved notice or decision through the case system and retain appeal or correction routes under existing agency procedures.

    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Case management system"

O->>S: Read application receipt and documents
    S-->>O: Ambiguous date extraction

diagrams.caption: An OCR error changes a material application date. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: An OCR error changes a material application date.
failures.detection: Field confidence and cross-document comparison disagree with the original page.
failures.recovery: Require staff verification of the source and rerun date-dependent checklist selection.

failures.scenario: A rule update is applied to an earlier application incorrectly.
failures.detection: Effective-date validation conflicts with the recorded application interval.
failures.recovery: Restore the applicable rule version and flag affected drafts for official review.

controls: Keep eligibility, benefit amounts, and adverse decisions under authorized official control.
Never convert missing documents into negative factual assertions about an applicant.
Provide inspectable source references and correction routes for extracted information.
Limit cross-agency retrieval by program purpose and approved access agreements.
Evaluate communication accessibility and language quality with affected user groups.

metrics.name: Intake preparation time
metrics.definition: Time from received application to caseworker-reviewable evidence and outstanding questions.

metrics.name: Extraction correction rate
metrics.definition: Material extracted fields corrected by staff divided by material fields reviewed.

metrics.name: Rule applicability accuracy
metrics.definition: Audited checklists using the correct program and date version divided by audited checklists.

metrics.name: Notice comprehension
metrics.definition: Applicants correctly identifying required next steps in a defined usability evaluation divided by participants evaluated.

tradeoffs.cost: Poor scans and unusual formats still require staff attention.
Policy transitions need explicit agency interpretation and migration handling.
Caseworker capacity continues to govern final disposition time.

rollout.acceptance: Staff and accessibility reviewers validate missing-evidence treatment, language quality, and date-sensitive rules.
One program compares draft packets with caseworker practice and tests cross-agency access restrictions.
Controlled notice drafts launch after correction, rule-transition, and appeal-route visibility checks pass.
